newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RIPKEN'S GRAND SLAM POWERS ORIOLES PAST ANGELS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RIPKEN'S GRAND SLAM POWERS ORIOLES PAST ANGELS.

text.p: Cal Ripken hit his sixth career grand slam to cap a six-run seventh, and Scott Erickson went eight-plus innings to raise his record to 5-1 as the Baltimore Orioles rallied for an 8-4 victory over Anaheim on Tuesday.
The Angels carried a 4-2 lead into the seventh but the Orioles sent nine batters to the plate and scored six runs -- five against starter Chuck Finley.

"Tonight I was able to come through with the bases loaded," said Ripken, who leads the Orioles with 28 RBI. "The idea is to relax in that situation, stay within yourself. If you get jumpy, you're not going to see the ball as well. "
Erickson (5-1) won his third straight start and improved to 13-2 lifetime against the Angels. He allowed four runs -- three earned -- and eight hits, walked two and fanned three.
Eric Davis was 4-for-4 for the Orioles.

In Boston, Jose Rosado allowed five hits in 7-2/3 innings and Jay Bell's RBI single snapped a tie and capped a three-run fifth inning, leading the Kansas City Royals to a 7-2 victory and a two-game sweep over the Boston Red Sox.
Rosado (3-0) allowed two runs, walked none and struck out seven. He has not allowed more than two earned runs in any of his seven starts and has pitched at least five innings each time.
In Cleveland, Julio Franco hit a three-run homer, and Orel Hershiser pitched seven strong innings as the Cleveland Indians defeated the Texas Rangers, 5-4.
Franco staked the Indians to a 3-0 start by homering off Rangers starter Roger Pavlik with one out in the first.
Hershiser (3-0) allowed two runs and seven hits. Eric Plunk was tagged for two runs in the eighth but Mike Jackson got the final five outs for his third save.
"The team picked me up," Hershiser said. "The innings I was bad, the team made some great defensive plays. It was a great team win."
In Milwaukee, Geronimo Berroa's bases-loaded single in the seventh inning snapped a 4-4 tie and lifted the Oakland Athletics past the Milwaukee Brewers, 6-5.
Berroa and Giambi each had a pair of RBI for the A's, who won for only the second time in their last six games. Jose Valentin went 2-for-4 with two RBI for Milwaukee.
Oakland first baseman Mark McGwire was ejected in the top of the first inning for arguing balls and strikes.
In New York, David Wells pitched an eight-hitter and the New York Yankees hit three home runs on the way to a 7-2 victory over the Minnesota Twins.
Wells (3-1) allowed two runs, walked one and struck out three in his second complete game of the season as he improved to 8-5 overall versus Minnesota.

"He will give us a lot of innings, he's a horse, no question about it," said New York manager Joe Torre about Wells. "When he goes out there he knows what his job is. It's not pressure, it's determination. He's a throwback, from the way he wears his uniform to the way he pitches."
"I only go out there every five days," Wells said. "I've got to out and give them seven solid innings.
In Toronto, Joe Carter drew a bases-loaded walk from Dan Miceli with two out in the bottom of the 10th inning, giving the Toronto Blue Jays their fourth straight win, 2-1 over the Detroit Tigers.
Tim Crabtree pitched a scoreless 10th, combining with Woody Williams on a four-hitter.
Toronto scored the go-ahead run via a bases-loaded walk for the second time in three games. It has not homered in 61 innings but also has not committed an error in 67.
In Chicago, Rich Amaral's two-run single in the top of the eighth inning capped a four-run comeback as the Seattle Mariners edged the Chicago White Sox, 7-6.
The Mariners began the eighth down, 6-3, but rallied back on an RBI double by Russ Davis, a run-scoring single by Alvaro Espinoza and Amaral's clutch single to right-centre field.

"He's very valuable to this team," Seattle manager Lou Piniella said of Amaral. "He puts the ball in play, has a good on-base percentage and gets the job done in the field. The reason he hasn't been playing every day that he's so valuable to me off the bench."
